onion.title: Onion Storage Techniques
content: Store onions in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated place.
Avoid storing onions in plastic bags as they need airflow to prevent spoilage.
Ideal storage temperature is between 10-15°C.
Keep onions away from direct sunlight to prevent sprouting.

tomato.title: Tomato Storage Techniques
content: Store ripe tomatoes at room temperature for best flavor.
Avoid refrigerating tomatoes as it can affect their texture and taste.
Keep tomatoes in a single layer to prevent bruising.
Store unripe tomatoes in a paper bag to speed up ripening.

potato.title: Potato Storage Techniques
content: Store potatoes in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated place.
Avoid storing potatoes in the refrigerator as it can cause them to turn green and produce toxins.
Keep potatoes away from onions, as they can cause each other to spoil faster.
Check potatoes regularly and remove any that are sprouting or rotting.

carrot.title: Carrot Storage Techniques
content: Store carrots in a cool, dark, and humid environment.
Remove the green tops before storing to prevent moisture loss.
Store carrots in perforated plastic bags to maintain humidity.
Avoid storing carrots near ethylene-producing fruits like apples.

apple.title: Apple Storage Techniques
content: Store apples in a cool, dark place with a temperature of 0-5°C.
Keep apples in perforated plastic bags to maintain humidity.
Avoid storing apples with vegetables, as they release ethylene gas.
Check apples regularly and remove any that are bruised or rotting.

banana.title: Banana Storage Techniques
content: Store bananas at room temperature until they ripen.
Once ripe, store bananas in the refrigerator to slow down further ripening.
Wrap the stems of bananas in plastic wrap to reduce ethylene gas emission.
Avoid storing bananas near other fruits, as they can cause them to ripen faster.

cabbage.title: Cabbage Storage Techniques
content: Store cabbage in a cool, dark, and humid environment.
Keep cabbage in perforated plastic bags to maintain humidity.
Avoid storing cabbage near ethylene-producing fruits like apples.
Remove outer leaves if they are damaged before storing.

garlic.title: Garlic Storage Techniques
content: Store garlic in a cool, dark, and dry place.
Avoid storing garlic in the refrigerator, as it can cause sprouting.
Keep garlic in a well-ventilated container to prevent mold.
Do not store garlic in plastic bags, as it needs airflow.

lettuce.title: Lettuce Storage Techniques
content: Store lettuce in the refrigerator at a temperature of 0-5°C.
Wrap lettuce in a damp cloth or paper towel to maintain moisture.
Avoid storing lettuce near ethylene-producing fruits like apples.
Do not store lettuce in airtight containers, as it needs airflow.

mango.title: Mango Storage Techniques
content: Store unripe mangoes at room temperature until they ripen.
Once ripe, store mangoes in the refrigerator to slow down further ripening.
Avoid storing mangoes near ethylene-sensitive fruits like bananas.
Check mangoes regularly and remove any that are overripe or rotting.
